title: Calculus and continuous optimization
summary: The calculus and optimization behind every model fit and every controller: Jacobians and Hessians, automatic differentiation, convexity and conditioning, gradient descent and its family, Newton and quasi-Newton methods, constrained optimization, and feedback control seen as an iteration.
objectives: Derive the Jacobians and Hessians of common ML functions and check them numerically
Explain forward- and reverse-mode automatic differentiation and their costs, and implement both on a small scale
Predict how step size and conditioning govern the convergence of gradient descent, and fix slow convergence by preconditioning
Implement momentum and Adam from scratch and choose an optimizer for a problem
Use Newton, Gauss-Newton and quasi-Newton methods with a line search, and know when second-order methods pay
Solve constrained problems with Lagrange multipliers, KKT conditions and projected gradient, and read multipliers as shadow prices
Analyse a discrete PI control loop as a linear iteration: stability from eigenvalues, tuning and anti-windup

build.title: Your first controller
build.summary: A supervisory controller for the simulator: a PI loop that resets the supply-air setpoint from the hottest rack inlet, chilled-water reset and economizer logic, scored against fixed setpoints and your own manual tuning, plus a chiller power curve fitted by nonlinear least squares.
